free_tier.stated: Hobby is $0 per month plus usage, with $10 of starter credits for 60 days (about 43 hours of Standard environments), 1 engineer, 3 projects, 4 concurrent vCPUs and 1 self-hosted runner; add a card anytime to pay as you go with no subscription.
free_tier.notes: The $10 credit is one-time and lasts 60 days, not renewing, so it is a trial rather than a recurring free allowance. Standard is 2 vCPUs and 8 GiB at $0.230 per hour on the pricing page; the limits reference lists $0.0504 per vCPU-hour and $0.0162 per GiB-hour past the allowance, which at 2 vCPU/8 GiB is $0.2376 an hour. The page is in public beta.

per_object_cap.stated: The largest single environment on Hobby is 2 vCPUs, 8 GiB and 50 GiB disk; agent files are capped at 50 MiB per file and 1 GiB per agent, bounded by the organization's 1 GiB file storage quota.

retention.stated: An agent's environment stops 5 minutes after its turn and is deleted after 2 days stopped unless extended up to 7 days on Hobby; inactive agents, transcripts and attached files are retained 90 days.

egress.terms: No sandbox egress price or allowance is stated on the pricing or limits pages; the pages price running vCPUs, memory and disk only. Static sites published by agents are included on every plan. Sandbox-level outbound traffic terms are unverified: behind a sign-up.

interface_detail: Agents are driven from the kosem app and CLI; the platform exposes LLM Gateway API endpoints and a documented REST API for quotas, while the microVM is reached through the agent environment rather than a published SSH endpoint.
tooling: the kosem app, the kosem CLI and the documented API; access connections for GitHub, AWS and Google Cloud; no SSH endpoint or rclone backend is published for the environment.
chaining: Each agent gets its own identity and short-lived, revocable credentials for GitHub, AWS and Google Cloud, and connects its own model accounts without a token markup, so a sandbox run can open a pull request or read cloud logs within granted scope.

limits.value: $10 of starter credits for 60 days, about 43 hours of Standard environments on Hobby
4 concurrent vCPUs and 16 GiB memory on Hobby, 20 environments, 100 GiB total environment disk and 1 GiB agent file storage
10 concurrent agents and 10 agent web page reads per minute per project on Hobby; LLM Gateway requests are limited to 1,000 per minute per project
stopped environments and disks are deleted after 2 days, extendable to 7 days on Hobby; an agent environment stops 5 minutes after its turn

limits_note: The Hobby plan allows 1 engineer, 3 projects, 2 model providers and 2 access connections. Starter credits run out after 60 days or when spent, and a card is needed to keep running.
binding_note: The $10 starter credit covering about 43 hours in 60 days binds before the 4 concurrent vCPU ceiling, because paid usage stops when the credit runs out and no card is held at signup.

identity_cost.detail: The sign-in page at app.kosem.ai/sign-in says 'Sign in or create an account.' and renders 'Continue with Google', a GitHub button, 'Sign in with a passkey' and an email field posting to /v1/auth/email/start; the page offers up to 20 passkeys. No phone or document field is visible, and no card is asked for before the $10 starter credit is used. Card details inside Billing are unverified: behind a sign-up.

reliability_note: Provider rate limits pass through to agents and their 429 responses are not smoothed by kosem. Stopped environments are deleted after 2 days unless extended to the plan cap, and environments whose billing account reaches $0 are deleted after a 14-day grace period.
confidence_note: Prices, starter credits, environment shapes and quotas are quoted from the vendor's pricing and limits pages read on 2026-11-25; the sign-in fields are quoted from the application's own sign-in script fetched the same day. Sandbox egress terms and in-account card flows are unverified: behind a sign-up.
